invariants.description: stage_tokenize must produce TokenizedDocument before stage_normalize can consume it as TokenizedDocument
invariants.rationale: Pipeline stages form a linear data flow; each stage's output type is the next stage's input type, enforcing transformation order

invariants.description: Every processing stage inherits from StageBase and implements process(data, config) -> list[OutputType]
invariants.rationale: A uniform stage interface enables the registry to load stages generically and allows middleware to wrap any stage

invariants.description: No stage module may import from any other stage module (stages communicate only via data passed by the runner)
invariants.rationale: Direct inter-stage imports would create hidden ordering dependencies and break stage isolation

invariants.description: No stage, adapter, or middleware may import from runner.py (no reverse dependency on orchestrator)
invariants.rationale: The orchestrator depends on stages, not the other way around; circular dependencies would make stages untestable

invariants.description: Adapter modules must not import from middleware modules (layer boundary: adapters wrap stages, middleware wraps execution)
invariants.rationale: Adapters and middleware operate at different abstraction layers; cross-layer imports would blur responsibilities

invariants.description: Utility modules must not import from each other (no circular dependencies in utils/)
invariants.rationale: Utility modules should be leaf dependencies; mutual imports would create import cycles and complicate testing

invariants.description: Validator modules must not import from stage modules (validators are called BY stages, not the reverse)
invariants.rationale: Validators are generic data checks; importing stage-specific logic would create circular dependencies and prevent reuse

invariants.description: Hook modules must not import from stage modules (hooks are lifecycle concerns, not data processing)
invariants.rationale: Hooks handle pipeline lifecycle (setup, teardown, error handling); coupling them to stage internals would break separation of concerns

invariants.description: Serializer modules must not import from stage modules (serializers work on output types only)
invariants.rationale: Serializers handle output formatting; they should depend only on data models and formatters, not on processing logic

invariants.description: Pipeline factory must not import stage modules directly (must go through the registry for stage resolution)
invariants.rationale: The factory should be stage-agnostic; direct stage imports would bypass the registry and hard-code pipeline structure

invariants.description: Legacy modules are dead code — no active module imports from them
invariants.rationale: Dead code is kept for reference only, not used at runtime

invariants.description: Every validator module exports a validate(data, config) function that returns a ValidationResult or raises ValidationError
invariants.rationale: A uniform validator interface allows stages to call any validator generically and enables validator composition

invariants.description: Every hook module exports an execute(context) function — the runner calls hooks through this uniform interface
invariants.rationale: A uniform hook interface lets the runner invoke any hook without type-specific logic

invariants.description: PipelineConfig.batch_size must be respected by all stages and the runner for consistent batch processing

structured.pattern: PipelineConfig.batch_size must be respected by all stages and the runner for consistent batch processing

invariants.rationale: Batch size is a global pipeline property; inconsistent batch handling between stages would cause data loss or duplication

invariants.description: StageRegistry must resolve stages in the order specified by PipelineConfig.stage_order

structured.pattern: StageRegistry must resolve stages in the order specified by PipelineConfig.stage_order

invariants.rationale: Config-driven stage ordering is the single source of truth; registry resolution must respect it to maintain pipeline semantics

invariants.description: Pipeline factory must apply all three middleware types (logging, retry, metrics) to ensure complete observability

structured.pattern: Pipeline factory must apply all three middleware types (logging, retry, metrics) to ensure complete observability

invariants.rationale: Missing middleware would create blind spots in monitoring or leave stages without retry protection

invariants.description: Lifecycle hooks must execute in order: pre_pipeline before stage processing, post_pipeline after, on_error on failure

structured.pattern: Lifecycle hooks must execute in order: pre_pipeline before stage processing, post_pipeline after, on_error on failure

invariants.rationale: Incorrect hook ordering would cause setup to run after processing or teardown to be skipped on error

invariants.description: Serializer output must consume the final stage's output type — the end-to-end type chain must be consistent
invariants.rationale: A type mismatch between the last stage and serializer would cause runtime serialization failures

invariants.description: Each processing stage is a separate module to enforce single responsibility and enable independent testing

structured.pattern: Each processing stage is a separate module to enforce single responsibility and enable independent testing

invariants.rationale: Separating stages allows each to be tested, replaced, or reordered independently; merging stages would couple concerns

invariants.description: Adapter modules provide a stable external interface for stages that may change their internal implementation

structured.pattern: Adapter modules provide a stable external interface for stages that may change their internal implementation

invariants.rationale: Adapters decouple external consumers from stage internals; stage refactoring doesn't break external code

invariants.description: Validators are separate modules because validation is a cross-cutting concern distinct from domain-specific transformation

structured.pattern: Validators are separate modules because validation is a cross-cutting concern distinct from domain-specific transformation

invariants.rationale: Embedding validation in stages would duplicate logic and make validation rules inconsistent across stages

invariants.description: Lifecycle hooks (pre/post/error) are separate modules because lifecycle management is distinct from data processing

structured.pattern: Lifecycle hooks (pre/post/error) are separate modules because lifecycle management is distinct from data processing

invariants.rationale: Inline lifecycle callbacks in the runner would couple lifecycle management to orchestration logic

design_rationales.question: Why is there a separate text_processor/models.py instead of defining data types within each stage?
design_rationales.answer: Centralizing data types in models.py prevents circular imports between stages and ensures type consistency across the pipeline.
downstream_effects: Moving types into stages would create circular imports
Type changes would require editing multiple files
Stages could no longer be tested independently

design_rationales.question: Why do all stages inherit from StageBase in text_processor/base.py?
design_rationales.answer: A common base class enforces a uniform process() interface, enables the registry to load stages generically, and allows middleware to wrap any stage without special-casing.
downstream_effects: Removing StageBase would break registry auto-discovery
Middleware would need per-stage wiring logic
Adding a new stage would require updating the runner

design_rationales.question: Why does text_processor/runner.py use text_processor/registry.py to resolve stages instead of importing them directly?
design_rationales.answer: Registry-based resolution allows stage ordering to be config-driven. Direct imports would hard-code the pipeline structure and require code changes to add, remove, or reorder stages.
downstream_effects: Direct imports would hide architecture from config
Stage ordering changes would require code edits
Dynamic stage loading (e.g., plugins) would be impossible

design_rationales.question: Why are there adapter modules wrapping some stages instead of exposing stages directly?
design_rationales.answer: Adapters provide a stable external interface. If a stage's internal implementation changes, only its adapter needs updating, not every external consumer.
downstream_effects: Direct stage access would couple external code to internals
Stage API changes would break all consumers simultaneously
Testing external integrations would require full stage setup

design_rationales.question: Why is logging/retry/metrics implemented as middleware modules rather than embedded in each stage?
design_rationales.answer: Middleware modules apply cross-cutting concerns uniformly. Embedding logging/retry in each stage would duplicate code and risk inconsistent behavior across stages.
downstream_effects: Per-stage logging would diverge in format and verbosity
Retry logic would be duplicated and potentially inconsistent
Adding a new cross-cutting concern would touch every stage

design_rationales.question: Why are validators in a separate subpackage instead of built into each stage's process() method?
design_rationales.answer: Validation is a cross-cutting concern: multiple stages share the same validation rules. Separating validators allows reuse, consistent error handling, and independent testing of validation logic.
downstream_effects: Embedding validation in stages would duplicate validation rules
Changing a validation rule would require editing multiple stages
Validation could not be composed or chained independently

design_rationales.question: Why does the pipeline use a factory module instead of constructing the pipeline directly in cli.py?
design_rationales.answer: The factory encapsulates the complex wiring of registry, middleware, hooks, and configuration. CLI, tests, and other entry points can create pipelines without duplicating setup logic.
downstream_effects: Without the factory, CLI and tests would duplicate wiring code
Adding a new middleware type would require changes in multiple places
Pipeline configuration would be scattered across entry points

design_rationales.question: Why are lifecycle hooks separate modules instead of callback functions inside the runner?
design_rationales.answer: Separate hook modules allow lifecycle behavior to be configured, replaced, or extended independently. Inline callbacks would couple lifecycle logic to the runner.
downstream_effects: Inline hooks could not be replaced without editing the runner
Testing lifecycle behavior would require full pipeline setup
Adding monitoring or alerting hooks would bloat the runner
